correctness.rationale: The base K_{p,q} Laplacian has four elementary invariant subspaces; for the 2-layer prism, L_G^+=L_base^+⊗P_+ +(L_base+2I)^−1⊗P_−. Direct currents for vertical edge sources yield exactly A,B and cycle values U,V=1+A/B−2R_eff. Horizontal sources fall into four base-edge incidence types with multiplicities 1,q−1,p−1,(p−1)(q−1); absolute cut and cycle sums are max(H₀,H₁) and max(1+H₀−2R_H,1+H₁−2R_H). I read the actual pinned verify_prism.py polynomial-region certificates and independently re-derived/recomputed 24 rational identities and nonnegative-coefficient polynomial witnesses plus all 31 finite pairs of the midrange; all passed. Separately built incidence matrices and orthogonal pseudoinverse projections for 10 (p,q) graphs, verifying every one of 410 edge columns, including exceptional (3,3) horizontal 73/30 and (3,7) phase disagreement. The polynomial certificates extend comparisons to all p≤q≥2, not finite extrapolation. Symbolically factored B−A and V−U to establish both switching thresholds.

value.rationale: The two distinct sharp extremizer-switching curves and a genuine exceptional balanced prism give a complete natural two-parameter spectral and Banach-operator invariant classification, not a trivial substitution into a single graph norm. It identifies when edge-orbit geometry controls cut versus cycle projections differently.

final_claim: For unweighted K_{p,q}□K₂, 2≤p≤q, the canonical cut projection Q and cycle projection C=I−Q on edge ℓ₁ satisfy ||Q||₁=max(A,B), ||C||₁=max(U,V) except p=q=3 where 73/30 is the horizontal cycle value. Vertical extremizers switch on distinct curves pq=2(p+q) and pq=4(p+q)+2, with A,B,U,V the explicit rational functions in RESULT.md.
limitations: Orthogonal graph Hodge projections only, not arbitrary linear projections
All edges unweighted and only one Cartesian K2 factor
